headline: South Asia: Islamabad set to host 2-day Makkah Defence Alliance meeting; Yemen conflict also on agenda
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Islamabad set to host 2-day Makkah Defence Alliance meeting; Yemen conflict also on agenda.
- Western Russia: Italian PM warns Ukraine after attack on Russian vessel in Mediterranean Sea.
- Africa: UN human rights chief warns of risk of escalating violence in western Nigeria.

Full breakdown follows.

United States - bottom line: Estimates of Russians killed in Ukraine surpass all combined US war deaths since WWI.
- Military Times, one day ago: Estimates of Russians killed in Ukraine surpass all combined US war deaths since WWI.
More than 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the war in Ukraine since Russia launched its full-scale war against the nation nearly five years ago.
- Military Times, one day ago: All USS George Washington CSG sailors returning from deployment to be provided ashore accommodations.
Sailors from the USS George Washington carrier strike group will be able to sleep in off-ship beds when they return from their roughly six-month deployment, the Navy said.
The Caribbean - bottom line: CMU trial could drag on until 2033, judge warns.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 23 hours ago: CMU trial could drag on until 2033, judge warns.
Senior Parish Court Judge Sanchia Burrell has warned that the trial of former Education Minister Ruel Reid and his co-accused could drag on until 2033 if the current pace of proceedings is maintained. Speaking yesterday in the Kingston and St Andrew Parish Court, Burrell pointed out that only about 10 to 11 of the 81 witnesses had so far given evidence, despite the matter having commenced in September 2025. “If the matter continues at this rate, we are not finishing this case until 2033,” Burrell warned.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Islamabad set to host 2-day Makkah Defence Alliance meeting; Yemen conflict also on agenda.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: Islamabad set to host 2-day Makkah Defence Alliance meeting; Yemen conflict also on agenda.
Pakistan is set to host a two-day meeting of the tripartite Makkah Defence Alliance’s top decision-making body from today, with discussions also expected to feature the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Houthi fighters in Yemen. The third session of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) is set to be held in Islamabad, where authorities have announced a public holiday today and imposed special movement restrictions in view of the high-level gathering. A local holiday has also been announced in Rawalpindi.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 21 hours ago: Security forces kill 12 India-sponsored terrorists in multiple IBOs in Balochistan: ISPR.
Security forces killed 12 India-sponsored terrorists in four separate intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan between November 20 and 23, the military’s media wing said on Thursday. According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), security forces targeted a terrorist hideout in Nushki district on November 20. Following an intense exchange of fire, eight terrorists belonging to the Indian-backed Fitna-al-Hindustan were killed. Weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the site, the ISPR added.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 15 hours ago: Meta battles political storm in India as Congress party sues, stages protests.
India’s main opposition party, the Indian National Congress, has sued Meta and the federal government, saying that an automated content-removal system is blocking political posts and images of ​opposition leader Rahul Gandhi ahead of state elections. The filing takes a week-long Congress campaign against Meta from the streets to the courtroom, and highlights Prime Minister ‌Narendra Modi’s automated takedown mandate, under which the Facebook and Instagram parent has restricted more than 5.4 million posts in the first half of 2026, up from about 70,000 in all of 2025.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 7 hours ago: AJK govt removes Rawalakot mayor over allegations of 'anti-state activities'.
MUZAFFARABAD: The Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) government on Thursday removed Rawalakot Mayor Abdul Naeem Khan from office and terminated his membership of the municipal corporation over his alleged “involvement in anti-state activities”. A notification issued by the Local Government and Rural Development Department said the action was taken under Section 23(2) of the Local Government Act, 1990. According to a separate notification by the AJK Home Department, dated Nov 15, Khan’s name was among those placed on the Fourth Schedule under Section 16 of the AJK Anti-Terrorism Act.

Both Italy and Kuwait confirmed the deaths, blaming the attack on Iran. But Tehran’s foreign minister Abbas Araghchi insisted in calls to his Kuwaiti and Italian counterparts that it was not behind the deadly strike. A court in Ukraine’s Moscow-annexed Donetsk region jailed a Colombian for 20 years, saying he was a mercenary fighting for Kyiv, Russia said on Thursday. The Russian Prosecutor General’s Office said the court “has handed down a verdict in the criminal case against 33-year-old Colombian national Cristian Morales Mendoza”, adding he was “a mercenary in an armed conflict”. Both Moscow and Kyiv have recruited thousands of foreigners in their armies since Russia launched its offensive in Ukraine...

Hong Kong is still healing, one year after a devastating inferno engulfed Tai Po’s Wang Fuk Court residential complex. Survivors are trying to move forward while grieving loved ones – parents, spouses, siblings and children – whom they lost without the chance to say goodbye. The South China Morning Post has created a full-page infographic to remember the 168 people killed in the fire. Tokyo is planning to introduce a new long-range anti-ship missile that could be launched from a broader range of vessels, according to Japanese media reports, potentially complicating Chinese military planning in a conflict. The proposed capability could allow Japan to equip vessels that traditionally do not carry anti-ship missiles, according to defence experts. Sharath Subramanian Shankar, a 28-year-old techie from Tamil Nadu, is implicated in sending over 1,500 hoax emails. These emails warned of attacks on significant locations in Mumbai, including the BMC office and the Bombay Stock Exchange. He was detained by Tamil Nadu police after returning from the US based on intelligence from Mumbai police. Another suspect, Ankit Shankhwar, is being investigated for supplying fake email accounts used in these threats.
